pillarForecast.why: Momentum fixes the 'turn on a dime' fiction, but grip 4 on a movement-only control is a big drop from 14; in narrow, dense late sectors the drift may feel like the ship's fault, not his. New fiction nits are possible (rocks passing through each other).
He still out-turns 300px/s pursuers that sweep ~130px per turn, so the clever-dodge feeling from run 19 survives, though it gets cramped in the narrowest lanes.
Ramp-in removes the cold-start wall, so sector-1 deaths should mostly vanish. B surges give a visible build/peak/release; A gives a steadier squeeze.
Eight pursuer-free seconds at the start of every run: welcome at first, possibly 'empty' by the fifth or sixth repetition.
A ~2-minute flight he nearly or actually finishes. Once he wins, expect him to ask what comes after the end.
Surge warnings are on-screen events, and rocks entering from beyond the walls are visible because the camera is centred on him.

biggestRisk: What's under his thumbs: the ship now slides (grip 4, ~0.5s to reverse) while lanes narrow to 400px, rocks get denser and walls still hurt. In Belt, Tumble and Breakout he'll see a gap, steer for it, and keep drifting into a rock or a wall; with two hits, deaths start to feel like the ship's fault rather than his mistake. Expect 'a bit too slidey in the tight parts' or a request to tune grip or lane width, not praise for the momentum he asked for.
abVerdict: Leans B (~55%) in what he says, because a surge is something he watches happen (flare, wave charging onto the screen, breaking away), while A's leashed wave sits just off-screen as a label. ~50% he never names a difference. If he does, it'll be a reaction to a surge moment ('that surge got me'), not a comparison. Outcomes may favour A (more wins), so a win in an A run could mask the preference.
